<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" />{{rh|CHA. XXIII.|ACCORDING TO S. LVKE.|209 HOLY weeke.}}</noinclude>{{sc|This is the king of the iewes}}. {{verse|chapter=23|verse=39}}† And one of those theeues that vvere hanged, blasphemed him, saying, If thou be Christ, saue thy self, and vs. {{verse|chapter=23|verse=40}}† But the other ansvvering, rebuked him, saying, Neither doest thou feare God, vvhere as thou art in the same damnation? {{verse|chapter=23|verse=41}}† And vve in deede iustly, for vve receiue vvorthie of our doings: but this man hath done no euil. {{verse|chapter=23|verse=42}}† And he said to {{sc|Iesvs}}, Lord, remember me vvhen thou shalt come into thy kingdom. {{verse|chapter=23|verse=43}}† And {{sc|Iesvs}} said to him, Amen I say to thee: this day thou shalt be vvith me {{sup|‖}} in paradise.

{{verse|chapter=23|verse=44}}† And it was almost the sixt houre: and there vvas made darkenesse vpon the vvhole earth vntil the ninthe houre. {{verse|chapter=23|verse=45}}† And the {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ This eclipse was seene and wondred at as a thing aboue nature, of Dionisius Areopagîta at Thebes, vvhen he vvas yet a Pagan. ''Dionys. ep. ad Polycarp. et ep. ad Apollophanen''.}}∷ sunne vvas darkened: and the veile of the temple vvas rent in the middes. {{verse|chapter=23|verse=46}}† And {{sc|Iesvs}} crying vvith a loude voice, said, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Ps. 30, 6.''}}* ''Father, into thy handes I commend my spirit''. And saying this, he gaue vp the ghost.

{{verse|chapter=23|verse=47}}† And the Centurion seeing that vvhich vvas done, glorified God, saying, In deede this man vvas iust. {{verse|chapter=23|verse=48}}† And al the multitude of them that vvere present together at that sight, and savv the things that vvere done, returned knocking their breasts. {{verse|chapter=23|verse=49}}† And al his acquaintance stoode a far of: and the vvomen that had folovved him from Galilee, seeing these things.

{{verse|chapter=23|verse=50}}† {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 27, 57. Mr. 15, 43. Io 19, 38.''}}* And behold a man named Ioseph, vvhich vvas a senatour, a good man and a iust, {{verse|chapter=23|verse=51}}† he had not consented to their counseil and doings, of Arimathæa a citie of Ievvrie, vvho also him self expected the kingdom of God. {{verse|chapter=23|verse=52}}† This man came to Pilate, and asked the body of {{sc|Iesvs}}. {{verse|chapter=23|verse=53}}† And taking it dovvne, vvrapped it in sindon, and laid him in a monument hevved of stone, {{sup|‖}} vvherein neuer yet any man had been laid. {{verse|chapter=23|verse=54}}† And it vvas the day of Parasceue, and the Sabboth drew neere. {{verse|chapter=23|verse=55}}† And the women that vvere come with him from Galilee, folovving after, {{sup|‖}} savv the monument, and hovv his body vvas laid. {{verse|chapter=23|verse=56}}† And returning they prepared spices and ointments: and on the Sabboth they rested according to the commaundement.

{{c|{{sc|Chap. XXIII.}}}}

''34. Forgiue them.''] A perfecte example of charitie in our Sauiour praying for his crucifiers, which the first martyr S. Steuen did folovv, ''Act. 7'': and the praiers of both were heard: Christs praier taking effecte in the Centurion and others, Steuens in Paul.<noinclude>{{rh||Dd|''43. In''}}</noinclude>
